bull.b: Reaffirmed revenue growth guidance indicates expanding commercial activity and continued demand for Surf Air’s regional, charter, and aviation services. If achieved, this scale can improve operating leverage, support investment in SurfOS and electrification, and strengthen the company’s competitive position over the next several quarters.

The Wheels Up agreement provides initial validation that SurfOS can be commercialized beyond Surf Air’s own airline operations. A multi-year enterprise software relationship could create higher-margin recurring revenue, diversify the business model, and establish a reference customer for additional aviation-industry contracts.

Strong On Demand growth, higher revenue per departure, and nearly doubled first-half private charter revenue suggest improving traction in the company’s more flexible aviation offerings. Gross-margin-positive new revenue lines could support a healthier mix and provide a durable path toward better unit economics.

bear.b: The magnitude of ongoing losses shows that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable operating profitability. Deteriorated gross profit and materially negative EBIT limit internal funding capacity, increase dependence on financing, and make future earnings improvement reliant on successful cost and mix changes.

Persistent negative equity weakens financial flexibility and leaves less capacity to absorb operating setbacks. Although debt has been refinanced, the remaining obligations and secured claims still create refinancing and capital-allocation pressure while continuing losses weigh on the company’s ability to repair its balance sheet.

Improved cash burn is constructive, but consistently negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not yet self-funding its operations and investment needs. Continued reliance on external capital can constrain strategic flexibility, increase financing costs, and amplify the consequences of execution shortfalls.
